newsitem.title: UK: Mark crosses firm but quiet, eyes on Dutch rates.
newsitem.headline: Mark crosses firm but quiet, eyes on Dutch rates.

text.p: The mark was moving with a firm tone against its European counterparts, but trading ranges were small as the currency market focused rather on the mark's moves against the dollar and sterling.

With the crosses lacking an overall theme of their own today amid what traders said was a quiet European calendar, the focus was on the Dutch central bank's special advances money-market tender scheduled for 1400 GMT today with speculation of a possible rise in the special advances rate.

"The guilder has come off its (near four-year) lows against the mark but it's not doing very much now... If there is a Dutch rate hike, it's likely to affect the mark against other currencies rather than mark/guilder itself," said a trader at a Japanese bank here.

A rate hike in the Netherlands would add fuel to the recent speculation that Germany might switch to variable rates for its repurchase tenders from the current fixed rates and allow rates to rise, traders and analysts said.

The latest bout of weakness in the Dutch guilder, which reached its lowest level in nearly four years against the mark earlier this week, had sparked expectations that the Dutch central bank may raise its special advances rate to shore up its currency. The rate is currently at 3.00 percent.
The guilder had recovered a bit from its multi-year lows of 1.127000 per mark reached on Tuesday, and was at 1.126275/6350 against 1.126250/6350 in late European trade on Wednesday.

Analysts said the relative health of the Dutch economy argued in favour of a rate hike, as did the fact that when the Dutch central bank last boosted the special advances rate by 10 basis points earlier this month, it said it had done so because of the guilder's weakness.
However, the guilder's recovery above 1.12673 per mark, its central rate in the European exchange rate mechanism, had slightly toned down expectations of a rate hike, they added.

"When the guilder rate went below the ERM midpoint, the market was beginning to think perhaps the Dutch central bank would need to give a signal to the market that they are taking the currency weakness seriously," said Stephen Lewis, chief economist at Monument Derivatives in London.
"But the guilder's recent recovery has helped to take the pressure off the Dutch central bank," he said.

Elsewhere in Europe, the Swedish Riksbank's board meeting today ended without any change in interest rates, as the market had expected. The mark was at 4.3400/30 Swedish crowns against its late Wednesday level of 4.3370/00.
The Bank of France is also holding its monetary policy meeting today, with a central bank repo tender due at 1115 GMT.
There was little market reaction to data showing France's unemployed rose by 17,400 in June to 3.13 million, resulting in a record jobless rate of 12.6 percent.
Mark/Paris was at 3.3710/15 against Wednesday's 3.3705/07, with traders noting very solid bids at around 3.3700.

Meanwhile, the mark was strengthening against the Swiss franc as the dollar rebounded against the Swissie after a slide earlier in the day. Mark/Swiss was at 82.67/70 centimes, off its morning low of 82.35 and against late Wednesday's 82.57/60.
